name: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Saguaro, dune rodents and the rain that drives a volcanic desert.

tip.title: Take away the rain
tip.text: Desert plants only grow when rain arrives. Set Rainfall to -100% and watch the saguaro and grasses, then the herbivores, then coyotes and bobcats.

sources.title: Wikipedia: El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense desert sunshine drives growth for every plant, but only where rain or stored water allows it.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Scarce, irregular rain in this part of the Sonoran Desert decides when plants grow, flower and set seed. Saguaro growth tracks rainfall closely.

nodes.name: Dune sand
nodes.desc: The Gran Desierto de Altar is North America's largest field of active sand dunes, a loose, fast-draining habitat for burrowers and specialised plants.

nodes.name: Soil microbes & detritivores
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the thin desert soil.

nodes.name: Saguaro
nodes.desc: Giant columnar cactus that stores rainwater. Its fruit feeds doves and ants, bats pollinate its flowers, and woodpeckers carve nest holes that other birds reuse.

nodes.name: Creosote bush
nodes.desc: Evergreen shrub that dominates much of the desert flats and hosts many specialised insects.

nodes.name: White brittlebush
nodes.desc: Silvery shrub with yellow flowers. GloBI has the master blister beetle recorded feeding on it.

nodes.name: Big galleta
nodes.desc: Tough bunchgrass of sandy and rocky desert ground, one of the main grasses available to grazers here.

nodes.name: Bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Wild sheep of the rocky peaks and cliffs. GloBI records it eating desert plants including a hedgehog cactus.

nodes.name: Sonoran pronghorn
nodes.desc: Endangered desert subspecies that eats mostly grasses and shrubs and copes with long spells without water.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: Large desert hare that browses grasses and shrubs and is prey for most of the area's carnivores.

nodes.name: Desert kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: Sand-dune rodent that eats mostly seeds and gets most of its water from metabolism. Prey for coyotes, bobcats and snakes.

nodes.name: White-throated woodrat
nodes.desc: Rodent that builds den middens and feeds on cacti and other desert plants.

nodes.name: Master blister beetle
nodes.desc: Large desert beetle that feeds on plants such as brittlebush, according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Armored stink beetle
nodes.desc: Flightless darkling beetle that scavenges plant litter and is a common ground insect on desert sand.

nodes.name: Pallid bat
nodes.desc: Large bat that hunts big arthropods such as beetles and scorpions, often taken on or near the ground.

nodes.name: Sonoran Desert toad
nodes.desc: Big toad that emerges after summer rains to eat insects and other small prey.

nodes.name: Sidewinder
nodes.desc: Small rattlesnake of loose sand that ambushes lizards and small rodents such as kangaroo rats.

nodes.name: Great horned owl
nodes.desc: Nocturnal raptor that takes rodents and rabbits across deserts.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Soaring scavenger that finds carrion by smell and sight over open desert.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Adaptable top predator. GloBI records it taking pronghorn, bighorn, jackrabbits, woodrats and kangaroo rats.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: Solitary cat of rocky desert and scrub that hunts rabbits, rodents and occasionally young pronghorn.
